title: The Recent Rise of Women Gun Owners
gist: RAND's analysis of General Social Survey data finds women's personal gun ownership jumped from 10% in 2018 to 15% in 2021 and 16% by 2024, while men's ownership stayed flat and sits below its level two decades ago - narrowing the gender gap in U.S. gun ownership from 29 points in 2004 to 19 points in 2024. The authors confirm the shift is real and broad-based across demographic and geographic subgroups, but say the public health and safety implications are still unknown.

insights.speaker: Rosanna Smart
insights.so_what: Quantifies the size of the pandemic-era demand shock that drove firearms industry revenue, and sets the base for durable aftermarket demand in ammunition, training and storage.

insights.claim: Previous reports of increased gun ownership among women have been overstated, but this analysis still confirms a genuine uptick that is widespread across geographic and demographic subgroups.
insights.speaker: Rosanna Smart
insights.so_what: Calibrates against hype: the trend is real but smaller than headlines claimed, and its breadth across subgroups makes it more likely to persist.

insights.claim: There are no administrative datasets capturing U.S. gun ownership or sales, so nationally representative surveys such as the General Social Survey are the best available evidence despite respondents potentially not knowing or not disclosing ownership.

insights.so_what: Any gun-ownership number in the market or policy debate is survey-derived and subject to disclosure bias - treat precise figures with a wide error band.
